explainerExcerptText: CHAPTER 1-10 SALES AND USE TAX. Source: Ord. 2008-5, Sec. 1 (2008); Ord. 2016-26, Sec. 1 SECTIONS: 1-1001. Definitions. 1-1002. Sales Tax Imposed. 1-1003. Use Tax Imposed. 1-1004. Gross Receipts of Alcoholic Beverages. 1-1005. Gross Receipts of New Farm Machinery and New Farm Irrigation Equipment. 1-1006. Exemptions. 1-1007. Collection and Administration. 1-1008. Contract with State Tax Commissioner. 1-1009. Dedication of Tax Proceeds. 1-1010. Grandfather Clause. 1-1011. Saving Clause. ____________________________ 1-1001. DEFINITIONS. All terms defined in Chapters 40-05.1, 57-39.2, 57-39.4, 57-39.5, 57-39.6, and 57-40.2 of the North Dakota Century Code (N.D.C.C.), including any future amendments, are adopted by reference. All references to the N.D.C.C. include amendments adopted by the North Dakota Legislative Assembly. 1-1002. SALES TAX IMPOSED. Subject to the provisions of N.D.C.C. § 40-05.1-06, and except as otherwise provided by this Ordinance, or the sales and use tax laws of the State of North Dakota, a tax of two percent (2%) is imposed upon the gross receipts of retailers from all sales at retail, including the leasing or renting of tangible personal property, within the corporate limits of the City of Harwood, North Dakota. 1-1003. USE TAX IMPOSED. Subject to the provisions of N.D.C.C. § 40-05.1-06, and except as otherwise provided in this Ordinance, or the sales and use tax laws of the State of North Dakota, an excise tax is imposed upon the storage, use, or consumption within the corporate limits of the City of Harwood, North Dakota, of tangible personal property purchased at retail for storage, use, or consumption in this City, at the rate of two percent (2%) of the purchase price of the property. An excise tax is imposed on the storage, use, or consumption within the corporate limits of the City of Harwood. 1-1004. GROSS RECEIPTS OF ALCOHOLIC BEVERAGES. Subject to the provisions of N.D.C.C. § 40-05.1-06, and except as otherwise provided in this Ordinance, a gross receipts tax of two percent (2%) is imposed upon all gross receipts from the sale of alcoholic beverages within the City. A person who receives alcoholic beverages for storage, use, or consumption in this state is subject to tax on storage, use, or consumption of those alcoholic beverages at the rate of two percent (2%). 1-10-2 1-1005. GROSS RECEIPTS OF NEW FARM MACHINERY AND NEW FARM IRRIGATION EQUIPMENT. Subject to the provision of N.D.C.C. § 40-05.1-06, and except as otherwise provided in this Ordinance, a gross receipts tax of two percent (2%) is imposed upon all gross receipts from the sale of new farm machinery and new farm irrigation equipment within the City. A person who receives new farm machinery or new farm irrigation equipment for storage, use, or consumption in this state is subject to tax on storage, use, or consumption of that machinery and/or equipment at the rate of two percent (2%). 1-1006. EXEMPTIONS. All sales, storage, use, or consumption of tangible personal property which are exempt from imposition and computation of the sales or use tax of the State of North Dakota are specifically exempt from the provisions of this chapter. 1-1007. COLLECTION AND ADMINISTRATION. Where not in conflict with the provisions of this Ordinance, the provisions of N.D.C.C. Chapters 40-05.1, 57-39.2, 57-39.4, 57-39.5, 57-39.6, and 57-40.2, and all administrative rules adopted by the Tax Commissioner, pertaining to the collection and administration of the retail sales, use, and gross receipts tax, including provisions for liability, refund, penalty, interest or credit, govern the administration by the North Dakota Office of State Tax Commissioner (hereinafter “Tax Commissioner”) of the taxes imposed by this Ordinance. 1-1008. CONTRACT WITH STATE TAX COMMISSIONER. The City Auditor for the City of Harwood is hereby authorized to contract with the Tax Commissioner for the administration and collection of taxes imposed by this chapter. The City Auditor has all powers granted the Commissioner and, in the absence of a valid contract with the Commissioner or failure of the Commissioner to perform the delegated duties, shall perform these duties in place of the Commissioner. 1-1009. DEDICATION OF TAX PROCEEDS. All fees, taxes, penalties and other charges imposed and collected under this chapter, less administrative costs, shall be dedicated and utilized only for infrastructure improvements, including publicly-owned utilities and buildings, job creation, business retention, expansion and recruitment. Proceeds collected pursuant to this chapter from such sales and use tax may be used to make direct payments of costs for the above purposes, or may be pledged to amortize bonds or other debt instruments which may be sold to finance such costs. 1-1010. GRANDFATHER CLAUSE. With respect to the purchase price of tangible personal property used by a contractor or subcontractor to fulfill a contract as defined in N.D.C.C. 57-40.2-03.3, the tax imposed by this section applies only to bids submitted on or after the effective date of this ordinance. 1-1011. SAVING CLAUSE. Should any section, paragraph, sentence, clause or phrase of this ordinance be declared unconstitutional, or invalid for any reason, the remainder of this ordinance shall not be affected thereby.

exactQuestion: This initiated Home Rule Charter Amendment, published in The Forum on August 25, 2026, would add a new Article X to the Home Rule Charter of the City of Harwood, North Dakota. The initiated amendment would impose additional significant requirements on the City of Harwood for certain development or building projects within the City. These requirements would place new limitations and obligations on how the City evaluates, approves, and administers development or building projects. The full publication in The Forum on August 25, 2026, outlines the specifics of those requirements. The full financial and operational consequences of the initiated amendment cannot presently be determined. The estimated fiscal impact of this measure is unknown.
explainerExcerptText: ARTICLE X The People further find that developments of extraordinary scale may create demands upon municipal infrastructure, transportation systems, utilities, emergency services, public finances, and natural resources that extend beyond those ordinarily associated with municipal land-use decisions and therefore warrant enhanced procedural review before discretionary municipal approvals are granted. The People further find that the long{erm public costs and benefits of Qualified Developments should be fully understood before discretionary municipal approvals are granted so that governmental decisions appropriately consider foreseeable impacts upon taxpayers, public infrastructure, municipal services, natural resources, surrounding properties, and future residents. Accordingly, the People adopt this Article to establish uniform procedures goveming the City's review and consideration of Qualified Developments requiring discretionary municipal approval. The provisions of this Article shall be interpreted to promote informed municipal decision-making, governmental transparency, fiscal responsibility, protection of public infrastructure, protection of natural resources, and the public health, safety, and welfare, consistent with the Home Rule authority granted to the City under the Constitution and laws of the State of North Dakota. Section 10.01. Purpose. The purpose of this Article is to establish uniform requirements governing discretionary municipal decisions concerning Qualified Developments. PUBLIC PROTECTION AND RESPONSIBLE MUNICIPAL DECISION.MAKING Section 10.00. Legislative Findings and lntent. The People of the City of Harwood flnd that certain developments, because of their scale, infrastructure requirements, resource demands, operational characteristics, or potential impacts, may substantially affect municipal infrastructure, public services, public safety, natural resources, community welfare, and the long-term flscal interests of the City. The People further find that discretionary municipal decisions concerning such developments should be based upon complete and objective information, independent professional evaluation, transparent governmental procedures, meaningful public participation, and written findings supported by substantial evidence. The People further find that informed municipal decision-making promotes responsible economic development while protecting the public interest, preserving municipal resources, and ensuring that significant public decisions are made only after the Governing Body has received sufficient information to reasonably evaluate foreseeable impacts upon the City and its residents. 1 This Article is intended to ensure that such decisions are based upon objective evidence, independent professional evaluation, transparent govemmental procedures, meaningful public participation, and written findings supported by substantial evidence. Nothing in this Article is intended to prohibit responsible economic development or to regulate matters reserved exclusively to the State of North Dakota or the United States. Rather, this Article governs the procedures by which the City exercises its own discretionary authority when considering Qualifi ed Developments. This Article shall be applied uniformly to all Qualified Developments without regard to the identity of the applicant, ownership structure, industry classification, or proposed business activity. The requirements established by this Article constitute minimum procedural protections governing discretionary municipal decisions concerning Quallfied Developments and shall be interpreted consistently with the City's Home Rule authority. Section'10.02. Definitions and Applicability. For purposes of this Article, the following definitions shall apply. I 0.02(A) Qualified Development. "Qualified Development" means a proposed lndustrial Development meeting the applicability requirements and impact thresholds established in this Section and requiring one or more discretionary municipal approvals from the City. A Qualified Development includes: 1. the construction ofa new lndustrial Development; 2. the expansion of an existing lndustrial Development; 3. a Substantial Modification of an existing lndustrial Development; or 4. any combination of related activities constituting a Common Development Plan. 10.02(B) lndustrial Development. "lndustrial Development" means any development involving industrial, manufacturing, processing, assembly, warehousing, distribution, energy production, utility-scale infrastructure, resource-intensive operations, high-intensity digital infrastructure, data processing facilities, or similar commercial or industrial activities that, because of their scale, operational characteristics, infrastructure requirements, or resource demands, may materially affect: o municipalinfrastructure; o public services; . transportation systems; o public safety; o natural resources; 2 . environmentalconditions; . surrounding properties; or . the general welfare of the community. Whether a development constitutes an lndustrial Development shall be determined according to its actual characteristics, anticipated operations, infrastructure requirements, and reasonably foreseeable impacts, and not solely by its name, business classification, ownership structure, zoning designation, or project description. 10.02(C) Governing Body. "Governing Body" means the City Council or any successor municipal legislative body lavrrfully authorized to exercise the legislative powers of the City under this Charter and the laws of the State of North Dakota. 1 0.02(D) Applicability. This Article applies whenever a Qualified Development requires discretionary approval, authorization, or action by the City of Harwood. Discretionary municipal action includes, but is not limited to: r annexation; o rezoning; o approval of a Planned Unit Development; o conditional use approval; e special use approval; . variance approval where authorized by law; r subdivisionapproval; o site plan approval; . development agreement approval; . infrastructureagreementapproval; o utility service agreements; o municipalfinancial participation; r tax incentives authorized by municipal action; . or any other discretionary governmental action necessary for the proposed development to proceed. Nothing in this Article shall be construed to apply solely because a ministerial permit or administrative approval is required. 10.02(E) Major lmpact Thresholds. A proposed lndustrial Development shall constitute a Qualified Development if it meets or exceeds any one of the following Major lmpact Thresholds. 3 (1) Electrical Demand. A projected peak electrical demand of 100 megawatts (MW) or greater, based upon reasonably foreseeable maximum operating conditions. Electrical demand shall include associated facilities and infrastructure reasonably related to the Common Development Plan. (2) Land Area. A total development area of 100 acres or greater owned, leased, controlled, or otherwise associated with the Common Development Plan. (4) Electrical Generation Capacity. lnstalled emergency, standby, backup, auxiliary, or other electrical generation capacity totaling 100 megawatts (MW) or greater. (5) Major Air Emissions Authorization. A development requiring a major source air quality permit, 1-itle V operating permit, or equivalent state or federal air quality authorization. 10.02(F) Moderate lmpact Thresholds. A proposed lndustrial Development shall also constitute a Qualified Development if it meets or exceeds two or more of the following Moderate lmpact Thresholds. 1. Projected peak electrical demand of 50 megawatts (MW) or greater. 2. Total development area of 50 acres or greater. 3. Projected water demand of 25,000 gallons per day or greater. 4, lnstalled electrical generation capacity of 50 megawatts (MW) or greater. 5. Air emissions requiring a state or federal air quality permit because of operational emissions. 6. Any additional threshold established by ordinance that is consistent with the purpose and intent of this Article and applies uniformly to all lndustrial Developments 4 (3) Water Demand. A projected water demand of 50,000 gallons per day or greater, or a projected demand exceeding five percent (5%) of the City's available municipal water supply capacity, whichever threshold is less. Water demand shall be evaluated using reasonably foreseeable peak operational conditions, including seasonal and emergency operating conditions where applicable. 10.02(G) Common Oevelopment Plan. "Common Development Plan" means two or more related phases, projects, parcels, facilities, structures, ownership entities, or operational components that are reasonably related by ownership, contractual relationship, shared infrastructure, common financing, coordinated planning, functional integration, or intended operational use. For purposes of determining applicability under this Article, all components of a Common Development Plan shall be considered collectively. A Qualifled Development shall not be divided into separate applications, ownership entities, construction phases, parcels, or operational components for the purpose or efiect of avoiding the applicability of this Article. 10.02(H) Substantial Modification. "Substantial Modification" means any expansion, alteration, replacement, addition, redevelopment, operational change, or infrastructure improvement that materially increases or creates new reasonably foreseeable impacts associated with an existing lndustrial Development. A Substantial Modification includes, but is not limited to, increases in: o electrical demand; o electrical generation capacity; . water demand; o wastewatergeneration; . transportationimpacts; o public infrastructure demands; . emergency response requirements; o air emissions; r land disturbance; o operational intensiV; or e other impacts materially affecting the public interest. Applicability shall be determined based upon the cumulative impacts of the existing development together with the proposed modification. 10.02(l) Cumulative lmpact Evaluation. ln determining whether a proposed lndustrial Development constitutes a Qualified Development, the City shall evaluate the cumulative and reasonably foreseeable impacts of the proposed development together with: 1. existing phases ofthe development; 2. approved but unconstructed phases; 3. planned expansions identified by the applicanl; 4. facilities constructed or proposed under a Common Development Plan; and 5. supporting infrastructure reasonably necessary for operation of the development. A development shall not avoid applicability under this Article through phased construction, incremental expansion, separate ownership entities, or multiple related applications. 1 0.02(J) lmpact-Based Applicability. The applicability of this Article shall be determined according to the actual and reasonably foreseeable characteristics, operational requirements, and impacts of a proposed development. The City shall not determine applicability solely upon: o the title or name of the project; o businessclassification' o ownership structure; o zoning designation; o parcel configuration; r application format; o constructionschedule; o financing structure; . corporate organization; or . any other administrative designation. The actual scale and anticipated impacts of the proposed development shall govern the determination of whether this Article applies. 1 0.02(K) Uniform Application. This Article shall be adminislered and applied uniformly to all Qualified Developments meeting the requirements established herein. Neither the identity of the applicant, ownership, industry classification, economic incentives, anticipated tax revenue, employment projections, nor any other economic consideration shall exempt a development from the procedural requirements established by this Article. Nothing contained herein shall prohibit the City from imposing additional requirements otherwise authorized by law where reasonably necessary to address unique impacts of a particular development. f 0.02(L) Supporting Infrastructure. For purposes of determining applicability under this Article, all infrastructure reasonably necessary to construct, operate, maintain, or support a Qualified Development shall be considered part of the development. Supporting infrastructure includes, but is not limited to: o electricalsubstations; t) . transmissionfacilities; . backup or standby generation; o cooling systems; o water supply infrastructure; . wastewater infrastructure; o stormwaterfacilities; o fuel storage and delivery systems; . intemal transportation infrastructure; r utility corridors; o parking and service areas; and o other facilities necessary for the intended operation of the development. Supporting infrastructure shall be evaluated together with the principal development when determining applicability and cumulative impacts. 1 0.02(M) Competent Professional Evidence. Whenever this Article requires determination of projected impacts, anticipated demand, operational characteristics, or other technical matters, such determinations shall be supported by competent professional evidence reasonably accepted within the applicable engineering, scientific, planning, or technical discipline. The City may rely upon information submitted by an applicant only after determining that such information is reasonably complete and, where required by this Article, has been independently evaluated by a qualified independent professional or other neutral third party when required by this Article. f 0.02(N) Construction of Thresholds. The impact thresholds established by this Article are legislative determinations adopted by the People of the City of Harwood to identify developments of extraordinary scale whose reasonably foreseeable impacts may exceed those ordinarily associated with municipal land-use decisions. The thresholds are intended solely to identify developments requlring enhanced procedural review before discretionary municipal approvals are granted. Nothing contained herein shall be construed to establish environmental standards, operational standards, or technical performance standards for any development. 10.02(O) Relationship to State and Federal Regulation. The procedures established by this Article are intended solely to govern the City's exercise of discretionary municipal authority. Nothing contained in this Article shall be interpreted as regulating matters exclusively reserved to state or federal agencies, including environmental permitting, utility regulation, occupational safety, or other matters preempted by law. 7 lnformation concerning such matters may be considered by the City solely for purposes of evaluating municipal impacts and exercising discretionary municipal authority. 1 0.02(P) Anti-Evasion. The provisions of this Article shall not be avoided through: . segmentation of a development into multiple applications; r successive ownership transfers; o division of property; o phased construction intended to remain below applicability thresholds; r creation of afiiliated entities; r modification of project descriptions; . changes in business classification; o changes in zoning designation; o or any other arrangement having the purpose or practical effect of avoiding application of this Article. Where the City determines that multiple applications, phases, parcels, or entities constitute a Common Development Plan, such components shall be evaluated collectively. The Governing Body shall evaluate the actual and reasonably foreseeable characteristics, operational purpose, and impacts of a proposed development rather than relying solely upon descriptions contained in the application or representations conceming the intended use of the project. f 0.02(O) Liberal Construction. This Article shall be liberally construed to carry out its stated purposes while remaining consistent with the Home Rule authority granted to the City under the Constitution and laws of the State of North Dakota. ln the event of uncertainty concerning applicability, the Governing Body shall interpret this Article in a manner that promotes informed municipal decision-making, transparency, and protection of the public interest, provided such interpretation remains consistent with applicable law. Section 10.03. Required Review Procedures. 10.03(A) General Requirement. Before granting discretionary municipal approval for a Qualified Development, the Governing Body shall ensure that the review procedures required by this Article have been completed and that the information required for informed municipal decision-making has been made available for public consideration. 8 No discretionary approval shall be granted until the Governing Body determines that the procedural requirements of this Article have been substantially satisfied. 1 0.03(B) lndependent Professional Evaluation. The Governing Body shall base its decision upon the administrative record developed pursuant to this Article, including competent professional evidence, and shall not rely solely upon studies, reports, analyses, projections, or representations prepared by or on behalf of an applicant or by persons having a direct financial interest in the approval of the proposed development. When technical information is necessary to evaluate reasonably foreseeable impacts of a Qualified Development, the City shall obtain an independent professional review by individuals or firms possessing appropriate education, training, experience, and professional qualifications. lndependent review may include verification, evaluation, peer review, or supplemental analysis of technical information submitted by the applicant. The purpose of independent review is to provide the Governing Body with objective professional evaluation sufficient to permit informed municipal decision-making. I 0.03(C) Selection of lndependent Professionals. lndependent professionals shall be selected by the City. The City may consult with the applicant regarding qualifications or scope of work but shall retain sole authority to select, direct, and supervise independent reviewers. Nothing contained herein shall prohibit the City from utilizing qualified governmental agencies, regional organizations, educational institutions, or independent consulting firms possessing relevant expertise. f 0.03(D) Applicant Responsibility for Review Gosts. The City may require the applicant to reimburse the Cig for the reasonable and necessary costs of independent professional review performed pursuant to this Aficle. Such reimbursement shall be limited to costs reasonably necessary to evaluate the reasonably foreseeable impacts of the proposed development and shall be applied uniformly to all Qualified Developments. Nothing contained herein authorizes the City to require unnecessary duplicative, or unreasonable studies or expenses. 1 0.03(E) Required Technical lnformation. The Governing Body shall obtain sufficient information to reasonably evaluate the foreseeable municipal impacts of a Qualified Development. I Depending upon the nature, size, and characteristics of the proposed development, such information may include professional evaluations concerning: 1 . municipal infrastructure capacity; 2. transportation and traffic impacts; 3. public safety and emergency response capabilities; 4" water supply and wastewater systems; 5. stormwatermanagement; 6. electrical infrastructure and utility demands; 7. environmental conditions affecting municipal interests; 8. fiscal impacts upon the City; 9. compatibility with sunounding land uses; 10. public service demands; 11. noise, vibration, lighting, or other operational impacts; 12. mitigation measures proposed to address identified impacts; and 13. anticipated facility closure, decommissioning, site stabilization, reclamation, long-term site management, and any reasonably foreseeable municipal responsibilities associated with the cessation of operations, including the removal or disposition of major infrastructure where applicable; 14. such other matters as are reasonably necessary to evaluate foreseeable municipal impacts. The Governing Body shall require only those studies or evaluations reasonably necessary to assess identified impacts that cannot otheMise be adequately evaluated using existing competent information. Where the Governing Body determines that reasonably foreseeable closure or decommissioning may result in material municipal obligations or long-term impacts, the Governing Body may require additional information concerning proposed decommissioning, reclamation, financial responsibility, or other tawful measures reasonably related to those impacts. 10.03(F) Public Notice, Public Participation, and Public Access. The Governing Body shall provide meaningful opportunities for public participation before granting discretionary approval for a Qualified Development. Public participation shall include, at a minimum: 1. public notice as required by law; 2. availability of non-confidential application materials and supporting documentation for public inspection within a reasonable time before the public hearing or final decision to permit meaningful public review; 3. at least one public hearing conducted before final discretionary approval; 4. reasonable opportunity for members of the public to present oral and written comments; 5. reasonable opportunity for questions directed through the Governing Body regarding technical information relied upon in the decision-making process; and 10 6. consideration of relevant public comments before final action is taken. Nothing contained herein shall prohibit additional public meetings, informational workshops, or other opportunities for public engagement whenever the Governing Body determines such participation would assist informed municipal decision-making. 10.03(G) Public Availability of lnformation. Except as otherwise protected from disclosure by state or federal law, information relied upon by the Governing Body in making a decision under this Article shall be made available for public inspection before final discretionary action. lf confidential or proprietary information is submitted to the City, the Governing Body shall require, whenever reasonably practicable, that non-confidential summaries, analyses, or substitute information be provided sufficient to permit meaningful public understanding of the proposed development and its anticipated municipal impacts. The existence of confidential information shall not prevent the Governing Body from obtaining sufficient information to satisfy the requirements of this Article. 1 0.03(H) Compleleness of lnformation. lf the Governing Body determines that information reasonably necessary to evaluate the foreseeable municipal impacts of a Qualified Development is incomplete, intemally inconsistent, unsupported by competent professional evidence, or otherwise insufiicient for informed municipal decision-making, the Governing Body shall defer final discretionary action until such deficiencies have been adequately addressed. Nothing in this subsection shall be construed as requiring certainty regarding future events; rather, decisions shall be based upon the best reasonably available competent professional information. o the application materials; . technical studies and professional evaluations; o independent review reports; . written public comments received; . hearing records; . written findings adopted pursuant to Section 10.04; and o other materials relied upon by the Governing Body in reaching its decision. The administrative record shall provide the factual basis supporting the Governing Body's exercise of discretionary municipal authority. 11 1 0.03(l) Administrative Record. The City shall maintain an administrative record documenting compliance with this Article. The record shall include: Section '10.04. Required Findings Prior to Municipal Approval. f 0.04(A) Written Findings Required. Before granting any discretionary municipal approval for a Qualified Development, the Governing Body shall adopt written findings of fact demonstrating compliance with this Article. The written findings shall be based upon the administrative record and supported by substantial evidence. The Governing Body shall not grant discretionary approval until the findings required by this Section have been adopted. 10.04(C) Gonsideration of Mitigation Measures. When reasonably foreseeable municipal impacts have been identified, the Governing Body shall consider mitigation measures proposed by the applicant, governmental agencies, independent professionals, or members of the public. 12 10.04(B) Required Findings. The Governing Body shall determine, based upon substantial evidence contained within the administrative record, that: '1. the review procedures required by this Article have been completed; 2. sufficient competent professional information has been obtained to reasonably evaluate the foreseeable municipal impacts of the Qualified Development; 3. independent professional review has been completed where required under this Article; 4. reasonably foreseeable impacts upon municipal infrastructure, public services, transportation systems, emergency response capabilities, public finances, and other municipal interests have been evaluated; 5. the Governing Body has considered relevant public comments received during the review process; 6. the Governing Body has considered reasonably foreseeable cumulative impacts associated with the Qualified Development; 7. the Governing Body has considered competent professional information concerning reasonably foreseeable facility closure, decommissioning, reclamation, longterm site management, and any reasonably foreseeable municipal impacts associated with the cessation of operations; 8. information relied upon in reaching the decision is supported by competent professional evidence; and 9. the Governing Body possesses sufficient information to exercise its discretionary authority in an informed manner. 1 0.04(D) lnsuffi cient lnformation. lf the Governing Body determines that the administrative record does not contain sufficient competent professional evidence to support one or more findings required by this Section, the Governing Body shall not grant discretionary municipal approval until such deficiencies have been adequately addressed. The Governing Body may continue proceedings, request additional information, direct additional independent review, or take such other lawful action as may be reasonably necessary to complete the administrative record. Nothing contained herein shall require denial of an application solely because additional information is required before an informed decision can be made. 10.04(E) Basis for Decision. The Governing Body's decision shall be based upon the administrative record developed pursuant to this Article. The Governing Body may assign such weight to the evidence as it deems appropriate, provided its findings are supported by substantial evidence contained within the administrative record. Nothing contained herein shall require unanimous professional opinions or eliminate the Governing Body's authority to exercise reasonable legislative judgment based upon conflicting competent evidence. 10.04(F) Written Decision. The Governing Body's final decision approving, conditionally approving, or denying a Qualifled Development shall be accompanied by written findings satisrying the requiremenls of this Article. The written findings shall identify the principal facts supporting the Governing Body's decision and shall reference the evidence relied upon in reaching those findings. 1 0.04(G) Uniform Application. The procedures and findings required by this Article shall be applied uniformly to all Qualified Developments. 13 Nothing contained herein shall require the Goveming Body to accept any particular mitigation measure. Consideration of mitigation measures shall not relieve the Goveming Body of its obligation to determine whether sufficient information exists to support informed municipal decision-making. Neither anticipated economic benefits, projected tax revenues, employment pOections, private agreements, nor other economic considerations shall excuse compliance with the procedural requirements established by this Article. 10.04(H) Scope of Review. exactQuestion: Shall the Home Rule Charter for the County of Oliver as approved and submitted to the electorate by the Oliver County Commission be approved?
explainerExcerptText: What is a Home Rule Charter? A Home Rule Charter is a voter-approved document that gives Oliver County broader authority to govern local matters, instead of relying only on the powers specifically granted by the North Dakota Legislature. It serves as the county’s “rulebook” for how it is organized and what powers it may exercise.  IT’S LOCAL Created for Oliver County and approved by county voters.  IT’S A PLAN Sets out the structure of county government and the powers the county may use.  IT’S OPTIONAL The county is not required to have a home rule charter. Voters decide. But does not automatically CREATE a sales tax. That must be voted on by the people in a future election after the home rule charter is voted in.  IT’S NOT UNLIMITED State law still applies, and there are important limits. The charter cannot override state criminal laws and must follow North Dakota’s home rule statutes. Quick Facts  On the ballot: Oliver County voters will decide whether to adopt a Home Rule Charter in the 2026 election.  Voter approval required: It only takes effect if a majority of county voters vote “Yes.”  Local control: Gives the county broader authority on county matters, such as land use, ordinances, and certain enforcement tools.  Not unlimited: Must follow the North Dakota Constitution and state law. Cannot conflict with state criminal laws, and certain subjects remain restricted.  Can be changed: Future amendments or repeal generally also go to voters.  Read the actual charter: The details matter. The specific powers in Oliver County’s proposed charter determine what changes, not just the phrase “home rule.” “Home rule gives local communities more say in local matters — and the responsibility to use that authority wisely.” — NORTH DAKOTA LEAGUE OF CITIES (APPLIES TO COUNTIES AS WELL) What Could Change If the Charter Passes? Depending on the powers included in the charter, Oliver County could have expanded authority in areas such as:  Land Use & Development More flexibility to create and enforce local land- use, zoning, and development regulations.  Ordinances & Enforcement Ability to adopt local ordinances and, in some cases, enforce them with penalties (within state law limits).  Finances & Taxes Potential authority for certain local taxes, fees, or other revenue tools (as allowed by the charter and state law).  County Government Structure Flexibility in how county offices operate, the roles and duties of officials, and other administrative matters.  Addressing Local Issues More ability to respond to county-specific challenges, such as energy development, data centers, infrastructure, and land stewardship. What Stays the Same? Even with a Home Rule Charter, these remain true:  State Laws Still Apply The county must follow the North Dakota Constitution and state laws, including criminal laws and eminent domain.  Cities and Townships Protected Home rule does not take away the authority of cities or townships within the county.  Voter Control You still have the right to vote on charter adoption, future amendments (in most cases), and county officials.  Public Meetings and Transparency Open meeting and public record laws still apply.  Your Property Rights State and federal constitutional protections for property rights remain in place.
